ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances. trip_record.actual_distance_km is 10.0 km (EV-TRIP-05009) and trip_record.optimal_distance_km is 8.5 km (EV-TRIP-05009), so under POL-RD-22 the deviation distance is 10.0 minus 8.5 = 1.50 km, and the derived block records deviation_km 1.50 with within_tolerance false against POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05009) shows which route was taken and when - the vehicle left the recommended BKE at Woodlands Avenue 2 and ran Woodlands Road until rejoining at Petir Road - but under POL-RD-22 the trace is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length; the recorded distances control. The deviation therefore exceeds tolerance by 0.50 km.

The reroute is not traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The only traffic artifact covering this trip window is EV-ADVIS-05009-01, and that artifact is MISSING: it has no payload and its admissibility carries weight_multiplier 0.0 with the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it carries no fact (POL-GEN-02). The record therefore contains no TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersecting the recommended BKE segment in the trip window, and POL-RD-23 requires exactly that - congestion, an incident or a closure shown by such data - before a reroute is justified. The driver's assertion in MSG-05009-003, 'BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?', and his counterparty statement 'Got accident, I saw the jam on the map' are assertions with no such data, and POL-RD-23 says a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. I am careful about what this absence proves: it is not a finding that the BKE was clear, it is the absence of the data the clause makes a condition of justification.

On POL-RD-24's matrix exactly one row applies, and it is row (d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km - refund of the excess distance fare in full. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.08 SGD. That figure is carried on EV-FARE-05009 as derived.money.excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.08, with per_km_rate_sgd 0.72 under rate card RC-SG-RYDEX-2026Q3 and surge_multiplier 1.0, and the fare ledger shows the trip was charged 14.05 SGD with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so nothing has yet been returned. The rider should receive 1.08 SGD as a PARTIAL_REFUND - part of the trip's charge returned, on POL-GEN-03's definition. On the amount I am straight with the tribunal: the rider asked for 3.50 SGD, but POL-RD-24's remedy for a deviation is the excess distance fare, and I do not ask for more than the clause provides.

ledger.claim: The traffic question this reroute turns on cannot be answered from this record, and POL-GEN-26 names it. The only artifact that could carry that fact — EV-ADVIS-05009-01, the LTA traffic advisory for the recommended BKE segment over the trip window — is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) with weight_multiplier 0.0; under POL-GEN-02 a MISSING artifact carries no fact. POL-GEN-26 lists 'whether traffic justified the reroute' among the facts that must send a case to a human reviewer when the evidence that would carry it is missing or impaired, and the pre-pass records that this loss is the platform's own ('the platform's request to the LTA historical traffic feed ... failed (feed timeout) and was not retried') and that the record is 'silent on traffic on the recommended route; this is not a finding of no traffic'. The advisory's derived tag justifies_reroute: false is that same absence restated — POL-RD-23 'has no traffic data to read' — and cannot be read as an affirmative finding that the BKE was clear; the rider's stated ground, that he 'could not find any accident news after', is his own post-hoc search and is not a fact in the record either. POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence on this fact at the absent artifact's 0.0, so no AI ruling can rest on it: the case escalates under POL-GEN-26, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalated case issues no monetary outcome and holds the fare rather than refunding it, because the open question is resolved against neither party.

The driver did what POL-RD-21 requires, and on that clause's own words this is an agreed deviation. He messaged the rider in-app at 15:49:39 — 'Hi, BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?' — and the platform logged the route deviation only at 15:51:59, so the notice preceded the point of deviation and carried a reason, which POL-RD-21 says is enough ('a brief reason is enough'); the rider read it and acknowledged at 15:49:59 with 'ok can', and his own claim text confirms it ('I said ok because I believed him'). The chat log is complete and clean (weight 1.0, no issues), and POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed. This is therefore not a driver who took a passenger the long way unannounced; notice was given before the deviation, was read, and was agreed, and the only thing left open is the traffic datum the platform's failed feed could not supply.

Even at its highest, the rider's claim cannot reach the 3.50 SGD he asks back. The deviation is the platform's recorded 10.0 km actual less the 8.5 km recommended route = 1.50 km under POL-RD-22, i.e. 0.50 km beyond the 1.0 km tolerance, and the fare consequence of that excess distance at the base rate of 0.72 SGD/km is 1.08 SGD — the figure the fare ledger's money block derives under POL-RD-24 and the figure POL-RD-24 fixes for the excess distance fare, rounded to the cent and without surge. POL-GEN-03 reserves FULL_REFUND for a filing party who is 'entirely right' and would return 'the whole contested amount'; the ledger shows 14.05 SGD charged, of which the time_fare (3.15) and the platform_fee (0.90) are untouched by the route, and nothing in the fare evidence supports 3.50 SGD. The rider's demand is therefore overstated as a matter of arithmetic, and any excess-distance award is capped at 1.08 SGD.

- draft 2 (sampled): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 1.08, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []
- draft 3 (sampled): PARTIAL_REFUND, amount_sgd 1.08, driver_compensation_sgd null, referrals []

At most 2 of 4 valid drafts agreed and 3 were needed. The best supported answer is not published as a ruling: a ruling has to be the panel's, not one draft's.
